content: 1. The metabolism of irinotecan may be reduced by glecaprevir/pibrentasvir, leading to an increase in its plasma levels or pharmacological effects. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 2. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir has the potential to increase the plasma concentrations of substrates of the Breast Cancer Resistance Protein (BCRP). Close monitoring is recommended. 3. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can elevate the levels or effects of liposomal irinotecan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (P-gp, also known as MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and patients should be monitored closely. 4. Isavuconazonium sulfate may increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting the P-gp efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 5. Isoniazid can increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by altering hepatic and intestinal metabolism mediated by the CYP3A4 enzyme. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 6. Istradefylline at a dose of 40 mg/day has been shown in clinical trials to increase the peak plasma levels and area under the curve (AUC) of CYP3A4 substrates. This effect was not observed at a dose of 20 mg/day. Istradefylline may also increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting the P-gp efflux transporter. Consider dose adjustments for sensitive P-gp substrates and monitor closely. 7. Itraconazole can increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting both the CYP3A4 enzyme and the P-gp efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 8. Ivacaftor and its M1 metabolite have the potential to inhibit P-gp, which may significantly increase systemic exposure to sensitive P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. Monitor patients closely when co-administering glecaprevir/pibrentasvir with ivacaftor. 9. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase the levels or effects of ivermectin by inhibiting the P-gp efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Ivosidenib may decrease the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative therapies should be considered. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor for a potential loss of therapeutic efficacy. 11. Ketoconazole can increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Lapatinib may increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by reducing its metabolism. Conversely, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase the levels or effects of lapatinib through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Larotrectinib may increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised. 14. Lasmiditan may increase the levels of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting the P-gp efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative therapies should be used. 15. Ledipasvir/sofosbuvir may increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting the P-gp efflux transporter. Conversely, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Leflunomide levels or effects may be increased by glecaprevir/pibrentasvir due to reduced metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Lenacapavir may increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by altering CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Additionally, lenacapavir may increase the systemic exposure of CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 18. Leniolisib, an OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 inhibitor, may increase the systemic exposure of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative therapies should be considered. 19. Lenvatinib levels or effects may be increased by glecaprevir/pibrentasvir through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Letermovir may increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters. Conversely, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase the levels or effects of letermovir by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
